167. It should not be thought that forms generate others similar to themselves in matter; for generation is proper to bodies, but it is the right and duty of the form to dispose seminal matter for generation by harmoniously moving its organs, to include within it a ray of light, or a secret spark of life, like a treasure, and to imprint its own specific character upon that life-giving <term>Spiritus</term> <gloss>spirit/breath</gloss> hidden in the seed. In the work of generation, through pulsing heat and at the appointed time, this unfolds itself into a <term>Anima</term> <gloss>soul/animating principle</gloss>, whether vegetable or animal, such that the spirit which had been secret and formal in the seed becomes the Form in the compound. Thus, what is hidden in the bosom of <term>Natura</term> <gloss>Nature</gloss> becomes manifest, and

<summary>This passage explains that biological forms do not reproduce themselves directly, but rather act as agents to organize matter and seed it with a vital spark that develops into a soul.</summary>
